newsitem.title: USA: GAO says US bank regulators should be consolidated.
newsitem.headline: GAO says US bank regulators should be consolidated.

text.p: The General Accounting Office on Wednesday recommended that the number of federal agencies responsible for banking oversight be reduced.

The congressional watchdog agency, after examining bank regulatory systems in five foreign countries, said that if Congress decides to modernize the existing U.S. system, consolidation of the regulatory responsibilities would be a logical step.

Specifically, it said that the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS), which oversees national thrifts, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which supervises national banks and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp (FDIC), which regulates federally insured, state chartered banks that are not Federal Reserve members, could be combined.

"This new independent agency, togther with the Federal Reserve, could be assigned responsibility for consolidated, comprehensive supervision of these banking organizations under its purview," the GAO report said.
It said the the U.S. central bank should have direct access to supervisory information as well as influence over supervisory decision making and the banking industry.

The GAO said this could be accomplished in a number of ways, including having the Fed keep its current oversight reponsibilities, or, alternatively, having it represented on the board of the new combined agency.

For its part, the Fed, in agency comments in the report, said it felt that the GAO shoud be specific in stating that the central bank needs "active supervisory involvement in the largest U.S. banking organizations and a cross-section of other banking institutions" to carry out is key central bank functions.

The report also said that Treasury Department needs access to supervisory information about the condition of the industry as well as the safety and soundness of banks that could affect the stability of the financial system.
Under the new structure, the FDIC, while losing its supervisory responsibilities, would continue with the necessary authority to protect the deposit insurance funds.
The GAO made its recommemdations after studying sytems in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Britain.
